summary: T. Ganapati Sastri was an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen in 1924. He served as curator at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (~1908–1924) and editor of the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series (~1908–1926).

T. Griffith Foulk works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1978–1987) under Luis Oscar Gómez, later teaching at Michigan (1987–1995) and Sarah Lawrence College (1995–2010; Riggs Professor around 2010).
T. K. V. Desikachar worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from around 1961 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. Matthew Ciolek is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and computational fields. He held positions at the Australian National University, including Social Sciences & Asian Studies Information Systems Administrator (attested 1994–1995) and a post attested in 2014.
T. N. Dharmadhikari was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under M. A. Mehendale. He served as the director of the Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala.

T. N. Ramachandran worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1925–1934) and later as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri and earned a PhD from the University of Madras. He served as librarian at the Adyar Library (~1926–1930) and senior lecturer in Sanskrit at Madras in 1933.

T. R. V. Murti was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, directed BHU's Centre for Advanced Study in Philosophy (~1953–1967), and taught at McMaster University (~1970–1975).
T. S. Devadoss is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who held posts at the University of Madras, where his affiliation is attested in 1994 and as a professor in 2008.

T. S. Eliot studied philosophy and other subjects at Harvard, Paris, and Merton College, Oxford, studying under George Santayana and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He later held posts at Birkbeck, University of London, and the University of Chicago (~1950).

T. S. Rukmani is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She held a post at Miranda House (attested 1983–1989) and served as Chairperson of Hindu Studies in the Department of Religion at Concordia University (attested 1989).

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where his career is attested in 1972, as professor from 1984 to 1992, and in 2007.
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who held positions at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as Pandit (attested 1993) and Professor (attested 2026).

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).
T. V. Vasudeva is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Deputy Director (attested 2026).

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a linguistics and Indology scholar. He completed undergraduate, master's, and doctoral studies at the University of Mysore, later serving on its faculty (lecturer 1968; professor 1984–1994) after teaching at Kanakapura, Bengaluru, and Osmania.

T. Venkatacharya was an Indology scholar who held an appointment at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (attested 1971) and served as a professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

T. W. Rhys Davids was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society, taught at University College London, and held the Chair of Comparative Religion at Manchester (1904–1915).
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed studies at the Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there as associate professor (1974, 1984–2000), directed the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (~2000–2008), and became professor at Ryukoku University (2002).
